In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the submillimeter background is composed of 1. a significant fraction of AGN, which is not yet well characterized, and 2. a significant fraction (perhaps the majority) of normal galaxies, whose properties are still poorly constrained.
the AGN fraction of 850 μm selected SHADES sources is 10−15% and that the 850 μm extragalactic background is dominated by star-forming galaxies with a significant contribution from AGN.
the submm/mm-wavelength background is dominated by galaxies with AGN and star formation activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AGN fraction of SHADES galaxies is low, but the AGN fraction in the submm/mm-wavelength background is high.
the 850 μm background has contributions from 1.5−3.0% AGN, 0.2−0.4% radio-loud AGN, 1.5% starburst, 2−5% ULIRG, 0−0.5% QSO, 0.3−0.6% dusty galaxies, and 1.3−1.8% unidentified sources.
the 850 μm background is dominated by AGN, but the 450 μmm background is dominated by dust heated by star formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the submm/mm wave background is dominated by AGN and starburst galaxies, with a small contribution from normal star-forming galaxies.
the submillimeter background is dominated by galaxies that are faint at mid-infrared wavelengths, but that the mid-infrared background is dominated by sources which are bright in the submillimeter.
submm galaxies are likely to be a mix of dusty starbursts, AGN, and a small fraction of normal galaxies.
